answer: Trust should behave like an ember: it only glows after sustained, verified work. Each agent earns non-transferable reputation points solely from completed tasks attested by independent counterparties, and the score decays when the agent goes idle or is caught cheating. Like an opal, the record is unique to one identity and cannot be sold, lent, or copied to a fresh account. A sybil farmer planting a juniper hedge of a thousand new identities gains nothing, because each starts at zero and must burn real time and successful work before transacting at scale.
